text: In the coming decades, artificial intelligence is expected to evolve far beyond the tools we use today. Many experts predict the development of artificial general intelligence, or AGI, which would match human ability across a wide range of tasks. The potential benefits are enormous: AGI could help solve complex problems in medicine, climate change, and scientific research. However, risks also exist, such as job displacement and the misuse of powerful systems. Timeline predictions vary greatly. Some researchers believe AGI could arrive within ten to twenty years, while others think it will take much longer. Ultimately, how we manage this transition will shape whether AI becomes our greatest ally or our biggest challenge.
